body.p: Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration of the claims in view of the following amendments and remarks. By these amendments, claims 1-8 and 10-11 are pending in the subject application, wherein claim 1 and 2 have been amended and claim 9 was canceled previously. Support can be found at least on paragraph [0044] of the publication of Application. Regarding the above amendment, no new matter is introduced.

The amendments set forth herein should not be interpreted to indicate that the Applicant has agreed with or acquiesced to the rejections set forth in the outstanding Office Action. The amendment to the claim has been made in an effort to lend greater clarity to the claimed subject matter and to expedite prosecution. Favorable consideration of the claims now presented, in view of the remarks and amendments set forth herein, is respectfully requested.
The Examiner alleges that the drawings are objected to under 37 CFR 1.83 (a) due to missing of features regarding the "interrogation signal" and "external interrogator".

As amended, the two features have been canceled from the claim(s), rendering the objection moot. Therefore, the Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and withdrawal of the objection of Drawings.
Claim 1 is allegedly objected to because of informalities.

As amended, the recitation of "coil provides an antenna" in line 1 has been amended into "coil serves as an antenna". Therefore, the Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejection of the claim 1.

In this Non-Final Office Action, claims 1-8 and 10-11 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) or 35 U.S.C. 112 (pre-AIA) since there is no description of how the power receiving coil generates power, as failing to comply with the written description requirement. Applicant disagrees.
Applicant respectfully submits that the specification of Application has already recited how the power receiving coil generates power and it is different from what Abreu teaches. Specifically,

the specification, in paragraph [0055], recites: the monitor pad 50 further includes: a power receiving coil 54 and a rectifying circuit 53. The power receiving coil 54 receives an external electromagnetic signal, and the rectifier circuit 53 converts the external electromagnetic signal into direct current. The direct current is supplied to the microphones Mic 1 and Mic 2 and the wireless transmission device 51 to supply power to them...an interrogation signal can be sent to the monitor pad 50 by an external interrogator. The power receiving coil 54 in the monitor pad 50 generates power for the microphones Mic 1 and Mic 2 and the wireless transmission device 51 in response to the interrogation signal. Since the principle of electromagnetic induction is well known to the person skilled in the art, on the basis of the foregoing recitation of the present disclosure, the person skilled in the art are able to readily conclude that the power receiving coil 54 receives an electromagnetic signal, such as an interrogation signal, and generates an alternating current based on the principle of electromagnetic induction, and that the rectifier circuit 53 converts the alternating current into a direct current.

Thus, the specification of the present disclosure actually discloses how the power receiving coil generates power and that this power generating design allows the monitor pad to draw energy from the external environment rather than receiving transmitted power from an external device as Abreu teaches. Therefore, Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejection of the claims 1-8 and 10-11.

The Examiner alleges that claims 1-8 and 10-11 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) or 35 U.S.C. 112 (pre-AIA) since ""an external processing device" (line 5) and "an external interrogator" (last line) are inferentially included and it is unclear if Applicant is positively reciting or functionally reciting the element".

As amended, "an external processing device" has been defined as "an external processing device for processing the body information", and "an external interrogator" has been deleted in claim 1, rendering the rejections under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) moot.

Besides, the present disclosure has already described how the monitor pad causes the power receiving coil to respond to a signal received by the monitor pad to "generator power". Specifically, the specification, in paragraph [0055], recites: the monitor pad 50 further includes: a power receiving coil 54 and a rectifying circuit 53. The power receiving coil 54 receives an

external electromagnetic signal, and the rectifier circuit 53 converts the external electromagnetic signal into direct current. The direct current is supplied to the microphones Mic 1 and Mic 2 and the wireless transmission device 51 to supply power to them...an interrogation signal can be sent to the monitor pad 50 by an external interrogator. The power receiving coil 54 in the monitor pad 50 generates power for the microphones Mic 1 and Mic 2 and the wireless transmission device 51 in response to the interrogation signal. Since the principle of electromagnetic induction is well known to the person skilled in the art, on the basis of the foregoing recitation of the present disclosure, the person skilled in the art are able to readily conclude that the key to the monitor pad 50 to generate direct current is to use the principle of electromagnetic induction, and it receives electromagnetic energy such as the interrogation signal through the power receiving coil, and converts it into stable direct current through the rectifier circuit for use by internal components. Therefore, the specification of the present disclosure has already disclosed how the monitor pad causes the power receiving coil to respond to a signal received by the monitor pad to "generator power".
Therefore, Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejection of the claims 1-8 and 10-11.

The Examiner alleges that claims 1, 3, 6-8, and 10 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Amoh (US2021/0244377) in view of Tran (US2008/0001735), Borelli (US2023/0238827) and LaBorde (US9,9677,865) or Abreu (US2015/0094914); claims 2 and 5 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Amoh in view of Tran, Borelli and LaBorde or Abreu as applied to claim 1 above, and further in view of Murphy (US2014/0101848); claim 4 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Amoh in view of Tran, Borelli and LaBorde or Abreu as applied to claim 1 above, and further in view of Blair (US2016/0294040) and/or Varshneya (US2003/0095263); claim 11 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Amoh in view of Tran, Borelli and LaBorde or Abreu as applied to claim 1 above, and further in view of Augustine (US10,201,935). Applicant disagrees. As an initial matter, Applicant respectfully submits that neither Tran nor Borelli discloses or suggest at least the features "at least a part of the power receiving coil serves as an antenna of the wireless transmission device". Even if the person skilled in the art were to modify Amoh in view

of Tran to use at least part of the power receiving coil as an antenna of the wireless transmission device or in view of the teachings of Borelli that the energy can be conditioned, which Applicant does not concede, such a combination still fails to arrive at the subject matter of the amended claim

Further, as amended, at least the features "the microphone comprises two microphones, which are symmetrical with respect to a center of the monitor pad and have an angle of 45 degrees with a short axis or a long axis of the monitor pad, respectively" of claim 1 are not disclosed, taught, or suggested by Amoh, Tran, Borelli, LaBorde, Abreu, Blair, Murphy, Varshneya, Augustine, or a combination thereof. Thus, the subject matter of the amended claim 1 is nonobvious over the cited references.
Accordingly, the Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejection of the amended claim 1 under 35 U.S.C.§ 103.

For at least above reason, Applicant respectfully submits that claim 1 and other pending claims depend directly or indirectly therefrom are patentably distinct over Amoh, Tran, Borelli, LaBorde, Abreu, Blair, Murphy, Varshneya, and/or Augustine.
In view of the foregoing remarks and amendments to the claims, the Applicant believes that the claims as currently pending are in condition for allowance, and such action is respectfully requested.

On the basis of the foregoing amendments and remarks, Applicant respectfully submits that the pending claims of the present application are allowable over the cited art. Entry of the amendments and remarks submitted herewith, and timely allowance of this application are respectfully requested. This Amendment is being made solely to expedite prosecution of the present application and does not constitute an acquiescence to any prior art, objections, or rejections identified by the Examiner. Should the Examiner have any questions, comments, or suggestions in furtherance of the prosecution of this application, the Examiner is invited to contact the attorney of record.
